title: The Words — Sc055: Darwin's pleading close-up, nested in one master symbol (94 frames)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: The nested-master pattern at its purest: the scene timeline is almost empty (one keyframe on the character layer, one on the background) and the whole 94-frame performance - a pleading, singing close-up that ends with Darwin falling out of frame - lives inside a single master symbol, 'DRW_marche + lente' (303 kf). Inside the nest, the face system does the acting: GB200_DRW_HEADCOMP carries 658 kf and the mouth comp 304 kf while the body barely moves. It also teaches name-vs-content discipline: the symbol is named for a slow walk, but the placed performance is a stationary emotional close-up - always trust the render over the filename.
notes: The entire scene is ONE placement: master symbol 'DRW_marche + lente' (303 kf, internal end frame 103) on the 'dwn' layer over GB214_WORDS_SC055_LO_BG.jpg. The scene timeline itself holds a single keyframe per layer - every gesture and face lives inside the nest.

Despite the symbol's name ('slow walk'), the rendered shot is a stationary pleading close-up: Darwin stays centre-frame singing/speaking, then falls out of frame - sheet frame 82 catches only his green-shoed legs kicking up, frame 94 is the empty corridor.

Performance arc from the sheet: serene eyes-closed (f1) -> worried open-mouth plea (f13-24) -> eyes-squeezed, hands-clasped singing (f36-47) -> anxious grimace (f59) -> sad sidelong plea (f71) -> collapse out of frame (f82-94).
